item.title: The Practice of Recovery — Tue Sep 22, 5:30 PM — Urban Well Yoga Studio
item.description: Tuesdays in September 15, 22 & 29 | 5:30 – 6:45 PM Led by Sarah Shelton, Urban Well Yoga Studio Coordinator, and The Reverend Stacey Carpenter, Associate Rector at Saint James The Practice of Recovery: Yoga, the 12 Steps and a Path for All is a three-week series exploring recovery, healing, and embodied practice in everyday life. This series is rooted in the wisdom of the 12 Steps, something that the co-founders of Alcoholics Anonymous believed everyone could benefit from. Recovery is not limited to one experience or one path. Many of us are recovering from something—alcohol or substance use, codependency, grief, stress, burnout, perfectionism, anxiety, illness, major life transitions, old patterns, or the places where we have felt disconnected from ourselves, others, our bodies, or a sense of meaning. item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Sep 22, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Capital Day — Sat Sep 26, 10:00 AM — Downtown Lancaster City
item.description:
Join us in Downtown Lancaster for Lancaster Capital Day, a free family-friendly celebration of local history, culture, and community. This festival recognizes Lancaster’s historic role as the nation’s capital on September 27, 1777, while exploring the people, places, and milestones that have influenced Lancaster County from Pennsylvania’s founding through today. Enjoy live music, artisan vendors, local food, cultural exhibits, historical demonstrations, and hands-on activities. There will be something for every age to explore!

item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: Ol Time Mtn Folk ‘n Northeast Pa Coal Mine Music presented by Jay Smar — Thu Oct 29, 6:30 PM — Lititz
item.description:
Music, Presentation, Everyone
An uplifting interactive program of”familial” folk, bluegrass, gospel, mountain and coal mine music performed with vocals accompanied by guitar, claw-hammer banjo, and to emulate the coal mining musicians of North East Pennsylvania, ....singing, fiddling and flat-foot clog-dancing simultaneously on a piece of plywood.....much audience involvement. N.E.Pa coal books, chronicles, pay scales, photos and related coal mining articles are also displayed at each performance for public view. This program is part of our annual Oehme Program Series. Online registration begins on 10/15.
